title: Turkey’s place in Europe – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: Podcast blurb: Mark Leonard and Aslı Aydıntaşbaş discuss her ECFR brief with Evren Balta casting Turkey as an 'embedded outsider' — a NATO member with the alliance's second-largest army, Ukraine supporter and nominal EU applicant that still keeps ties with Moscow. Short summary page; no detailed arguments in the text.

insights.claim: Turkey is an 'embedded outsider': it maintains relations with Moscow and other Western adversaries while being a NATO state with the alliance's second-largest army, supporting Ukraine and technically applying for EU membership.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Turkey's dual alignment makes it a swing actor in Black Sea and Ukraine diplomacy.
insights.locator: In their brief, Aslı and Evren

insights.claim: At the July NATO summit he hosted, Erdogan gave visiting leaders Turkish-made revolvers loaded with live ammunition, symbolising Turkey as an ally no one can place.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta, Mark Leonard
insights.so_what: Illustrates Ankara's assertive, ambiguous posture within the alliance.
insights.quote: a gift no one could accept from an ally no one can place
insights.locator: In their brief, Aslı and Evren

insights.claim: Turkey plays a role in Ukrainian and Black Sea diplomacy, and the open question is how far a shared agenda exists between Ankara and Europe.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta, Mark Leonard
insights.so_what: Turkey-EU alignment affects Black Sea shipping and Ukraine settlement prospects.

source_meta.author: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta, Mark Leonard
